summary: This is a calendered Li-ion negative electrode made mostly of flake/platelet graphite (~68% of the section, 10-30 um long, long axes horizontal, so the vertical axis is probably through-thickness). It is blended with ~9% of angular 2-10 um Si-containing particles, most likely SiOx and/or Si/C (brighter in BSE, speckled in Inlens; EDS needed to confirm), which are locally clustered in the upper centre. The carbon-binder domain is patchy, filling interstitial pockets and enriched around the Si-bearing particles, while many graphite faces are separated by bare slit pores; larger voids concentrate in a centre/centre-right band. Visible porosity is ~15%; the automated 9.7% captures only the black, empty pores and is a lower bound, because the unfilled pores expose buried material that thresholds as solid. Damage is limited to basal-plane cracking, kinking and local fragmentation of graphite and rare cracking of Si-bearing particles; among the automated metrics, bright_particle_area (10.5%) is roughly right but slightly high, whereas bright_raw, the particle count and the median size are biased by noise, edge rims and small fragments.

This is a calendered graphite/Si-based (most likely SiOx) blended anode, seen in an ion-polished, non-infiltrated cross-section. Flake-like graphite (~10 um equivalent diameter, 12-25 um long, ~72% of area) dominates and is preferentially aligned horizontally, so vertical is probably the through-thickness direction. Angular Si-phase particles (~1-17 um, ~11% of area) and patchy nanoporous carbon-binder pockets occupy the interstices. Visible 2D porosity is ~14%, mostly slit-like inter-particle gaps. Because pores are unfilled and partly show subsurface material, the automatic 6.2% pore fraction is a lower bound; the filtered bright-particle fraction (13.6%) is roughly right to slightly high, while bright_raw (21.6%) is inflated by edges. Damage is limited to basal-plane cracks in graphite, occasional cracked or partly debonded Si-phase particles and local CBD agglomeration; the main artefacts are pore see-through, Inlens edge brightening, mild curtaining and a rough unpolished zone at the top-left.

This is most likely a calendered graphite-based negative electrode blended with ~7-8% area of angular 0.5-9 µm high-Z particles consistent with SiOx/Si, embedded in a thin, partly nanoporous carbon-binder domain. Graphite flakes (~15-30 µm long, 6-12 µm thick) are flattened and strongly aligned horizontally, so vertical is the through-thickness direction; they show frequent basal-plane cracks and slit-like interparticle gaps or debonding. Resolvable porosity is low (~6%), mostly horizontal slits concentrated in the middle and lower part, while CBD-rich nanoporous pockets cluster in the upper third and bright particles cluster locally. The automatic bright-phase metrics (6.7%, 61 particles, median ~3 µm) agree well with the images. The 5.7% pore value matches the visible black voids but is a lower bound on true porosity, because of CBD nanoporosity, shine-through in unfilled pores and possibly hidden binder/resin-filled space. Diagonal curtaining/polishing streaks, local charging and Inlens edge saturation are present but barely affect the BSE-based metrics.

This is a calendered graphite anode with a minor (~4-5 area%) population of angular, high-BSE-yield particles 1-6 um across, most likely Si or SiOx, dispersed uniformly between horizontally aligned graphite flakes (vertical = through-thickness; the whole 52 um height lies inside the coating). Packing is dense with slit-like, laterally connected pores; visual 2D porosity is ~12%, so the automatic 8.2% is a lower bound because open pores showing subsurface material read grey in BSE. The bright-phase threshold metrics (4.1-5.1%, ~49 particles, median 2.55 um) agree with visual inspection, though sizes are biased low. Several Si-type particles show grey shells, small gaps or Inlens charging, and a few have a granular texture; whether these reflect coatings, cycling-related alteration or preparation cannot be decided without EDS or sample history. Preparation and imaging artefacts (diagonal curtaining in ETD, Inlens edge glow and an upper-left dark zone) are present but do not compromise the BSE-based analysis.

This is a calendered graphite anode blended with ~6-7 % (area) of angular Si-based particles, most likely SiOx (typical section size ~3.5 um, granular nanotexture, often wrapped in 0.5-1 um low-Z shells), evenly dispersed between horizontally aligned graphite platelets 5-30 um long. Pores are flattened slits parallel to the flakes and are largely open (not resin-filled), so the BSE threshold (9 %) underestimates sectional porosity, which is visually ~15 %. The bright-phase metrics (5.7-7.4 %, 62 particles, median 2.8 um) are reliable to within ~1-2 percentage points, with sizes biased low by sectioning and fragment exclusion. Damage is minor to moderate: one clearly cracked and a few mottled Si-based particles, basal-plane slits in graphite and some debonding around Si particles; whether the electrode has been cycled cannot be determined from these images.

This apparently ion-milled, non-impregnated cross-section shows a densely calendered graphite anode. Flake/lens-shaped graphite particles ~10-30 um long make up ~77% of the section and are stacked with long axes horizontal, so the vertical direction is very likely through-thickness. About 5% of the area is a moderately BSE-bright, angular 2-7 um additive, most plausibly SiOx or a Si-C composite (EDS needed). It is unevenly distributed, enriched on the right, and several particles show rims and debonding gaps. Porosity is dominated by horizontal slit pores: the BSE threshold value of 9.8% matches the visibly black area but is likely a lower bound (~13% resolvable), while the bright-phase metrics (5.2-6.4%, 43 particles) agree well with the images. The carbon-binder domain is patchy and visible only in Inlens, which also suffers from strong charging and edge effects and should not be thresholded.

This is a calendered graphite-based anode with ~6 area-% of bright, angular Si-based particles (likely SiOx or Si; EDS needed). They are dispersed among flattened, horizontally aligned graphite flakes typically 10-30 um long, plus one oversized ~35 um spheroidised graphite particle with internal voids. The section is not resin-infiltrated, so the 8.8% BSE pore fraction captures only deep open voids; a visual estimate of the 2D void fraction is ~13%, dominated by slit pores parallel to the flakes and a void cluster in the centre. The carbon-binder domain is sparse and identifiable only by texture in Inlens/ETD, appearing as thin films and a few binder-rich patches. The automatic bright-particle metrics (5.7%, 36 particles, median 3.5 um) agree well with the images, whereas bright_raw is inflated by edge rims and scratches; several Si-based particles show partial gaps to the matrix, and graphite shows basal-plane cracking whose origin (calendering versus cycling) cannot be determined.

This is a calendered graphite-based anode containing a minor (about 5-6% area) dispersed Si-based additive, most likely SiOx, which appears in BSE as angular bright particles of 1-7 um among densely packed, horizontally aligned graphite flakes. The carbon-binder domain is visible mainly in Inlens, as porous clusters in interstices and thin, partly detached films around particles. Visible porosity is about 15%, mostly slit-like gaps along flake boundaries plus a few larger cavities, concentrated in the upper third where SiOx and CBD are also enriched. Graphite shows internal basal-plane cracks, and some SiOx particles show shells, patchy interiors or cracks, but the pristine vs cycled state cannot be determined. The automatic bright-phase metrics (5.2-6.4%, 40 particles, median 3.7 um) are reliable, whereas the 10.5% pore fraction is a lower bound because the pores are unfilled and their floors read as solid.

This is an interior cross-section of a dense, strongly calendered graphite-based anode. About 77% of the area is flake-like graphite aligned horizontally (vertical = through-thickness), plus ~4% of angular high-Z particles that are most likely (carbon-coated) SiOx/Si, concentrated in the right third. The carbon-binder domain forms thin fringed films on most graphite surfaces plus a few 2-6 um porous agglomerates, and the resolved porosity (~10-11%) is mainly horizontal slit pores with a few larger voids. The automatic BSE metrics are credible for the bright phase (~3.9%) and for resolved black pores, but porosity is a lower bound and the carbon-binder domain cannot be separated from graphite in BSE. Inlens shows a strong non-compositional dark band in the upper third that should not be used for segmentation, and the Si identity and cycling state need EDS or reference data to confirm.

This is a calendered graphite-based anode in which large, flattened graphite flakes (~72 % area, 10–30 µm long, aligned horizontally, so the image vertical is the through-thickness direction) dominate. About 9 % of the area is smaller (2–9 µm, median ~4 µm) angular BSE-bright particles, most likely a Si-based additive (SiOx/Si; not confirmed by EDS). Packing is dense: section porosity is ~14 %, the automatic 9.3 % being a lower bound because open pores show grey subsurface floors. Pores are mainly horizontal slit-like gaps plus a few 3–8 µm voids, and the carbon-binder domain forms patchy nanoporous pockets concentrated around the bright particles. Several Si-based particles are cracked or fragmented, and some show nanoporous textures and darker layered rims, which could reflect calendering damage or cycling-related degradation; the electrode history cannot be determined from these images, and the main imaging artefacts (unfilled pores, Inlens edge saturation, mild ion-milling curtaining) significantly affect only pore quantification.

Sample epqdaau9 is a densely calendered graphite anode on a Cu foil (visible at the bottom edge). About 6 area% of angular, higher-Z Si-based additive particles (likely SiOx and/or Si-C, 1-9 um) are dispersed in the interstices of large, horizontally aligned graphite flakes (10-40 um). Porosity is mainly slit-like and parallel to the current collector, concentrated in a mid-thickness band. Black voids account for ~7% of the area, but including open pores with visible subsurface material the in-plane porosity is ~11-14%. The carbon-binder domain forms thin films and nanoporous pockets, best seen in Inlens and somewhat concentrated around Si-phase particles, while graphite flakes show abundant basal-plane fissures. The automatic bright-phase metrics are reliable to within ~1% once the Cu strip is masked, whereas the threshold pore fraction is a lower bound; diagonal curtaining and Inlens banding mainly affect the topographic detectors.

This is a polished cross-section of a calendered graphite-based anode, most likely a graphite/SiOx (or Si) blend. About 73% of the area is low-Z flaky graphite (long axes ~10-35 um, strongly aligned parallel to the electrode surface, with internal cleavage cracks), and ~5-6% is bright, dense, angular particles of 1-10 um (median ~3 um, plus a few granular ones) sitting in the interstices between flakes. The carbon-binder domain is sparse and visible only in Inlens, as thin films and small lacy patches often around the bright particles. Porosity is slit-like, laterally connected and aligned in-plane; because the pores are not resin-filled, the automatic 8.2% is biased low and a visual estimate is ~17%. The structure is fairly uniform laterally, the bright-particle threshold metrics are broadly reliable, and the main artefacts are oblique curtaining streaks, sub-surface signal in open pores, the unpolished top strip and faint tile seams.

This is a calendered graphite-based anode cross-section (175 x 52 um, entirely within the coating) dominated by horizontally aligned flake graphite 10-45 um long. It also contains ~4 area% of angular higher-Z particles that are most likely Si or SiOx, a minor population of granular intermediate-brightness particles, and a patchy nanoporous carbon-binder domain concentrated in the interstices. Resolved in-plane porosity is ~14-16%, dominated by slit pores parallel to the flakes and a semi-continuous horizontal void chain ~18-25 um below the top edge. The automatic 11.4% pore fraction is a lower bound because the pores are not resin-filled and sub-surface material is counted as solid; the bright-particle metrics (4.0%, 41 particles, median 2.5 um) agree with visual inspection, while the raw bright fraction (6.0%) is inflated by edges. A striking Inlens-only contrast between black and grey graphite by region points to a surface-potential, connectivity or lithiation-state difference that cannot be resolved from these images; EDS and the cell history are needed to confirm the Si phase and interpret this contrast.

Sample rxax5ozo is a densely calendered graphite-based anode. Flattened flake/lens-shaped graphite particles (typically 15-35 um long, 5-12 um thick, ~70% of the area) are strongly aligned with long axes horizontal, so the vertical image direction is most likely through-thickness. About 5% of the area is a BSE-bright, angular 2-7 um phase consistent with a Si-based additive (SiOx or Si/C), clustered in CBD-rich interstices; about half of these particles have a porous/granular interior and several are fractured or carry lower-Z caps, which may be intrinsic or cycling-related. The CBD forms thin films and small nanoporous pockets, porosity is mostly in-plane slits between flakes, and the automatic bright-phase fraction and count are reliable (sizes slightly low), while the 8.9% pore fraction is a lower bound and ~14% 2D porosity is a better estimate.

This is a calendered graphite-based Li-ion anode in which large (8-30 um), strongly horizontally aligned graphite flakes make up most of the solid, together with a minor (~5% area) population of angular, BSE-bright 1-9 um particles that are most plausibly a Si-based additive such as SiOx (EDS needed to confirm). The carbon-binder domain is visible mainly in Inlens as bright lacy material filling interstices and wrapping the Si-based particles. Porosity consists of flake-parallel slit pores plus larger interstitial voids, with moderate packing heterogeneity (looser upper-centre and lower-right regions). Because the pores are not resin-filled, subsurface material appears grey in BSE and the automatic 14.9% pore fraction underestimates the true section porosity (~20-28%); the bright-particle metrics (4.7%, 46 particles, median ~2.6 um) agree with visual inspection, whereas bright_raw (7.2%) is inflated by edge rims. The main artefacts are see-through open pores, curtaining/polishing striations and Inlens edge brightening; damage is limited to internal basal-plane cracks, frayed flake edges and inter-flake slit gaps.

Sample 71vgq3fw is a graphite-dominated negative electrode with a minor, well-dispersed higher-Z additive (most likely SiOx, ~6% of the section area) that appears as angular 1-8 um shards in the interstices between 3-25 um irregular graphite flakes. The graphite flakes are densely packed with a preferred near-horizontal alignment (vertical is probably through-thickness), contain lenticular basal-plane cracks, and are wrapped by a carbon-binder network that is resolved only in the Inlens image. Open porosity consists mainly of horizontally elongated slit pores and a few in-plane fissures up to ~25 um long. The BSE-threshold porosity of 8.5% captures only the deep voids; total porosity is more likely ~15-20%, because unfilled pores showing sub-surface material are counted as solid. The bright-particle metrics (5.8%, 54 particles, median 3.1 um) agree with visual inspection, while the raw bright fraction is inflated by rims and edge pixels, and the rims, gaps and internal texture of several Si-bearing particles cannot be attributed to coating, preparation or cycling from these images alone.

This is a calendered Si/graphite blended anode cross-section. Large, partially horizontally aligned graphite flakes (~68% area, 10-35 um) form a dense, interlocked framework, and ~55 angular, higher-Z Si-based particles (likely SiOx; ~5-6% area, ~3 um median section diameter) fill the interstices; a minority of these have a speckled/porous texture. Porosity is mainly slit-like and flake-aligned, and because the pores are not resin-filled the automatic BSE pore fraction (12.5%) is an underestimate; the true value is likely ~20-25%. The bright-particle metrics (5.4% area, 54 particles, median 2.96 um) agree well with visual inspection and can be trusted. Graphite shows internal cracks and frayed edges and a few Si particles show interfacial gaps, while imaging is affected mainly by curtaining in the SE channels and sub-surface signal in open pores; the cycling state cannot be determined from these images.

This section shows the upper ~50 µm of a calendered graphite anode, imaged from the free surface downward. It is blended with a minority (~6-7% of the section, ≈8% of solids) of angular, higher-Z Si-containing particles of 2-7 µm, most likely SiOx. Graphite flakes 10-25 µm long are densely packed and preferentially aligned in-plane, with slit-like inter-flake pores, basal-plane cracks, frayed ends and a few long horizontal gaps; the Si particles are evenly dispersed, but some sit in gaps with poor contact and two show internal streaks or porosity. Because the pores are not resin-filled, the BSE threshold porosity (9.7%) captures only deep voids and underestimates the visually estimated ~20%, whereas the bright-particle metrics (5.9%, 56 particles, median 2.8 µm) are broadly trustworthy. The particle-wise dark band and top-edge charging in the Inlens image are imaging effects rather than compositional differences, so Inlens should not be intensity-thresholded.

This is a calendered graphite-based anode with a minor (~4-5 area%) Si-based additive, most likely micron-sized angular SiOx, and a carbon-binder domain visible mainly in Inlens as bright, spongy films and interstitial pockets. Graphite flakes (~10-35 um long, 5-12 um thick) are densely packed and strongly aligned horizontally, so the vertical direction is probably through-thickness; pores are slit-like and in-plane, and basal-plane cracks/delamination are common inside particles. The automatic bright-phase metrics (3.9-5.7 area%, 47 particles, median 2.4 um) agree with the images and can be trusted. The 9.7% pore fraction is a lower bound because the pores are not resin-filled and recessed pore floors are counted as solid; I estimate ~18% porosity. The structure is uniform at the field scale with moderate local heterogeneity (fines/CBD/Si-rich pockets and a central band of larger voids), and no clear cycling damage can be identified.

This is a non-resin-infiltrated, ion-polished cross-section of a graphite-based Li-ion anode containing ~5% (area) of a brighter, higher-Z additive that is most likely SiOx/Si: about 50 angular-to-rounded particles, typically 2-4 µm and a few up to ~10 µm. The graphite consists of platelet flakes ~15-25 µm long and 4-12 µm thick, strongly aligned horizontally by calendering and showing frequent intra-particle basal-plane slits; vertical is most likely through-thickness, although neither current collector nor surface is visible. Porosity is estimated at ~25%, made up of aligned slit pores plus large voids concentrated in the centre and a horizontal upper band; the automatic 14.7% is an underestimate because unfilled pores expose deeper surfaces with graphite-like BSE grey. The bright-phase metrics (4.4-5.4% area, 50 particles, median ~2.6 µm) are broadly reliable, with small biases from the 2 µm² cut-off and one mottled low-contrast particle, while the carbon-binder domain is visible only in Inlens as discontinuous lacy patches at particle necks.

Sample kbdh4tri is a cross-section of a graphite-based Li-ion anode with ~6% (area) of angular, higher-Z particles 2–7 µm across, most likely SiOx (chemistry needs EDS confirmation), dispersed evenly between densely packed, flattened graphite flakes 10–25 µm long. Graphite long axes are moderately aligned with the horizontal, suggesting vertical is through-thickness, and many flakes contain lamellar slit cracks and frayed edges. The pores are not resin-filled, so much of the ~25% in-plane porosity shows subsurface particles at graphite-like BSE grey levels; the automatic pore fraction (8.6%) captures only deep voids and is strongly underestimated. The bright-particle area (5.6%) and count (64) are reasonable, the raw bright fraction (10.3%) is inflated by edges and noise, and the binder is visible only qualitatively in Inlens as thin films lining the particles.

This is a calendered graphite-based anode cross-section with a minority (~6-7 area%) Si-containing additive, likely SiOx or Si (to be confirmed by EDS), imaged entirely within the coating. Flake graphite platelets 10-30 um long are densely stacked with long axes near horizontal, so vertical is most likely the through-thickness direction. The flakes contain basal-plane cracks, are separated by a network of thin crack-like gaps, and are wrapped by a lacy CBD that covers almost every particle. The 1.5-9 um Si-phase particles show dense and granular textures and sit in graphite interstices, but they are concentrated on the right side of the field, with a few fractured or partly debonded particles. The automatic bright-phase metrics (6.3%, 47 particles, median 2.7 um) are trustworthy as 2D statistics, whereas the 9.8% pore fraction is a lower bound because the pores are not resin-filled; I estimate ~16% visible porosity.

Sample pl8uabbv is a calendered graphite-based anode: ~70% of the section is aligned platelet graphite (10-40 um long) and ~5-6% is a dispersed, higher-Z population of angular 1-8 um particles that are most likely SiOx or Si/C (EDS needed to confirm). The strong horizontal flake alignment makes the vertical image axis the through-thickness direction; pores are mostly aligned, largely unfilled slits, and the CBD collects in pockets around the Si particles rather than coating the graphite uniformly. Visual section porosity is ~15%, above the 9.7% BSE-threshold value because shallow open pores showing sub-surface material are counted as solid, whereas the bright-particle metrics (4.9%, 64 particles, median 2.5 um) agree well with the images. The microstructure is fairly uniform apart from a top-left corner with large voids, nodular agglomerates and Inlens-dark graphite, and the graphite shows widespread interlamellar cracking; curtaining and tile-stitching artefacts are present but minor.

This is a dense, apparently heavily calendered graphite-based Li-ion anode containing ~5 area-% of a brighter, angular Si-based additive, most likely SiOx (not confirmed without EDS). Graphite flakes (10-40 um long, aspect ratio 2-4) are strongly aligned horizontally. The 1-8 um Si-based particles are evenly dispersed in the interstices, and the carbon-binder domain forms a discontinuous lacy web seen mainly in Inlens. Porosity is mostly thin in-plane slits plus a few triple-junction voids, notably beside a large debonded central graphite particle; visible 2D macroporosity is ~13%, so the automatic 8.4% is a lower bound because the unfilled pores have grey floors in BSE. The automatic bright-phase metrics (4.6%, 39 particles, median 2.5 um) are trustworthy. Damage is limited to graphite edge exfoliation, internal slits, a few fractured or mottled Si-based particles and local debonding.

Sample tuy3zymq is a densely calendered graphite-dominant anode containing ~5% (area) of a BSE-bright, angular Si-based additive (likely SiOx or micron Si, 1.5-6 µm) dispersed in the interstices between horizontally aligned graphite flakes (~10-25 µm long). The graphite shows abundant basal-plane cracking and frayed edges, and the carbon-binder domain, visible essentially only in Inlens, forms wispy films concentrated in interstices and around Si particles, while long inter-flake slits are largely bare. The section appears ion-milled without resin infiltration, so open pores expose subsurface material: the automatic 9% porosity is a strong underestimate (visual ~22%), the cleaned bright-particle metrics (5.2%, median 2.3 µm, 69 particles) are credible, and the raw bright fraction (11.1%) is inflated by edges and noise. The microstructure is fairly uniform across the field (heterogeneity 2/5), and whether the cracking reflects calendering, cycling or preparation cannot be decided from these images.

Sample ufdvpb81 is an ion-milled, non-resin-infiltrated cross-section of a graphite-dominated anode containing ~5% (area) of brighter, angular Si-based particles, probably Si/SiOx or a Si/C composite. Graphite flakes 10-25 um long are densely packed with moderate sub-horizontal alignment, extensive basal-plane cracking and slit-like inter-particle pores; vertical is likely the through-thickness direction. The Si-based particles occur as dense and mottled/porous variants, often with thin low-Z rims and partial debonding. They are unevenly distributed: ~7% in the right half versus <1% in the lower-left quadrant. The automatic bright-phase area and count are reliable and the median size is slightly low. The 12.4% pore fraction underestimates the ~15-20% visual porosity, because sub-surface material in open pores reads as solid.

This is a graphite-dominated anode containing ~5-6% (area) of bright, angular 2-7 um Si-based additive particles (most likely SiOx/Si; composition unconfirmed), in a densely packed network of graphite flakes and potato-shaped particles whose long axes lie mostly horizontally (vertical is probably through-thickness). The carbon-binder domain is sparse, consisting of thin films on particle surfaces plus small carbon-black clusters, and is visible mainly in Inlens because it matches graphite in BSE. Visible porosity (~13%) consists of slit-like interflake gaps concentrated in a central mid-height band and the lower left; graphite basal-plane cracks, shells around Si-rich particles and a few porous Si-rich particles may indicate cycling, though this cannot be confirmed. The automatic BSE bright-phase area (5.1-6.3%) is credible, but its median particle size is biased low and the 9.8% pore fraction should be treated as a lower bound.

Sample vc2whyaq is a calendered graphite/Si-based (Si or SiOx) blended anode. About three quarters of the section is flattened, strongly horizontally aligned graphite flakes (1-35 um, typically ~15 um long), and ~6% is angular, BSE-bright Si-based particles (2D median ~2.8 um) dispersed in the interstices, many with thin low-Z rims. Porosity is open (not resin-filled), slit-like and anisotropic, concentrated in horizontal inter-flake bands; the BSE threshold value of 9.6% is a lower bound and the 2D porosity is more likely ~15%. The carbon-binder domain is sparse and patchy, seen mainly in Inlens as nanoporous pockets at flake junctions and around Si-based particles. Damage is limited to graphite cleavage cracks, one semi-continuous horizontal gap band and a few cracked Si-based particles; the automatic bright-phase metrics are reliable, while the pore metric is biased low.

This is a calendered graphite/silicon-based blended anode: ~72% of the section is graphite flakes 10-30 um long with long axes mostly horizontal, so the vertical axis is probably through-thickness, plus ~7% angular BSE-bright Si/SiOx particles (~3 um median, up to ~8 um) in the interstices, a sparse nanoporous carbon-binder domain, and ~14% open, mostly slit-like porosity in horizontal bands. Many Si-based particles show 0.3-1 um low-Z rims, internal mottling, cracks or core-shell gaps, which could indicate a carbon shell or cycling-related degradation; the electrode history cannot be determined from these images, and the elemental identity needs EDS. The automatic bright-phase area and count are reliable and the sizes slightly low, while the 9.5% pore fraction is likely an underestimate because the pores are unfilled and show sub-surface material. Heterogeneity is moderate (3/5), driven mainly by uneven Si distribution and banded porosity.

Sample x7u69zsw is a densely calendered graphite-based anode with a minor (~7 area%) fraction of a higher-Z, most likely SiOx/Si-based additive (identification not confirmed without EDS). Flattened graphite platelets, typically 10-25 um long, are strongly aligned with the horizontal (in-plane) axis and closely interlocked, and they often show lenticular basal-plane cracks and fragmentation. The angular 1-9 um bright particles sit isolated in interstices; some are partly debonded and some have a mottled, possibly porous interior. The binder domain forms thin lacy films and webs resolved clearly only in Inlens, and the pores are unfilled slits and interstitial voids. The automatic bright-particle metrics are credible, but the 8.3% BSE pore fraction underestimates the visible porosity (~15%) because sub-surface material in unfilled pores reads as solid, and the 10.7% raw bright fraction is inflated by edge effects.

This sample is a calendered graphite-based Li-ion anode blended with ~5 area-% of an angular high-Z additive, most likely Si or SiOx, imaged as a 175 x 40 um strip inside the coating with no current collector or surface in view. Lenticular/flake graphite (10-40 um long) dominates, aligned mostly parallel to x (y is very likely through-thickness) but with domains tilted 20-40 deg, slit-like interparticle pores and frequent lamellar internal cracks; the Si-based particles (section median ~3.3 um, up to ~9 um) sit in CBD-rich interstices, are concentrated in the upper half, and a few are fractured or mottled/porous. The section is not resin-infiltrated, so the BSE threshold captures only the deep pores (9.4%) whereas the true porosity is probably ~20-30% (best estimate ~25%). The filtered bright-particle metrics (5.1%, n=30) match the images well, bright_raw (7.2%) is inflated by edge rims, and the CBD is visible only in Inlens, where it cannot be cleanly separated from pore-back topography.
